key_insight: Unifying crystal databases expands the reach of screening known materials while exposing overstated novelty in inverse-designed crystals.
engineering_relevance: Structure-matched records and property models can help engineers identify overlooked candidates and assess whether generated materials are genuinely new.
method: Match crystal structures across 55 databases into a source-traceable, self-extending database.
Train CGTNet, an equivariant graph transformer, to predict missing material properties.
Audit screening candidates and compare screening with stiffness-conditioned generation at equal verification budgets.
evidence_signal: The database contains 14.6 million crystals and 131.8 million property values; generation yielded 100 stiff hits versus screening’s 55, but all generated hits contained osmium and 82 repeated recorded compositions.
watch_item: Only 4.5% of crystal-property pairs have recorded values, so predicted candidates still require validation, and repeated compositions alone do not establish structural duplication.
paper_title: Probing the limits of forward screening and inverse design of crystal materials
